summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented with post-dialysis hypotension and weakness after skipping his antihypertensive medication. He was evaluated in the emergency department with initial blood pressure of 84/32 mmHg, elevated lactate of 2.6, and mild leukocytosis. His symptoms improved with supportive care, and he remained hemodynamically stable throughout the admission. A chest X-ray showed chronic interstitial lung disease without acute findings. He did not require additional dialysis or procedures. The patient was discharged home the following morning with instructions to resume his medications after dialysis and follow up with his nephrologist, with no acute infections or complications identified.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Hemiplegia and hemiparesis following cerebral infarction affecting right dominant side
